title: Editor Anatomy 🏗️
description: Tour every major panel and understand how they work together.

slides.title: The Big Picture 🖼️
slides.content:
# What Makes Up the Editor?

Unreal Engine's interface is **fully modular** – every panel can be moved, stacked, or hidden. But the default layout gives you these core areas:

* **Menu Bar** (top) – File, Edit, Window, Help
* **Toolbar** – quick actions: Save, Play, Build
* **Viewport** – your window into the 3D world
* **Content Browser** – asset management hub
* **World Outliner** – list of all actors in the level
* **Details Panel** – properties for selected actors
* **Modes Panel** (left) – placement tools (landscape, foliage, etc.)
* **Output Log** (bottom) – debug messages

*Analogy:* Each panel is like a different tool in a carpenter’s belt – you swap between them as needed, but they’re all within reach.

quizData.question: Which panel is used to browse and manage your project's files?
quizData.explanation: The Content Browser is your asset manager. The World Outliner lists actors in the level.

slides.title: Docking & Undocking 🔗
slides.content:
## Move Panels Like Magic

* **Drag a tab** by its name to move it anywhere.
* **Dock** it to the edges of the editor or to another panel's title bar.
* Create **stacked tabs** – e.g., place Content Browser next to World Outliner.
* **Undock** a panel into a floating window – great for dual‑monitor setups.
* Right‑click a panel tab → **Hide Tab** to remove it from view.
* Restore via **Window** menu at the top.

**Try it:** Drag the **Content Browser** tab to the right side of the viewport and dock it vertically.

quizData.question: Once you hide a panel, you cannot bring it back.
quizData.explanation: All panels can be re‑enabled from the Window menu at the top of the editor.

slides.title: Panel Relationships 🤝
slides.content:
## How Panels Work Together

* **World Outliner** + **Details Panel** = select an actor in Outliner, edit it in Details.
* **Content Browser** + **Viewport** = drag an asset from the browser directly into the viewport.
* **Modes Panel** + **Viewport** = click a mode (e.g., Paint) then paint in the viewport.

This is why the default layout groups these panels nearby – **context switching is instant**.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Reset to Default

If you’ve moved panels into a mess, go to **Window → Load Layout → Default Editor Layout**. It instantly restores the clean arrangement.
